clue.text: One who's accepting large tip, holding ace

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it gripped inside, so one letter sits within the other words

blocks.note: fat means large or bulky
to list is to tip or lean to one side, as a ship does
A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A tolerant waiter or caddie happily pockets a big gratuity while clutching an ace card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, but here it is the verb meaning to lean over, as a listing ship does.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes events are predetermined, so such a person resigns themselves to whatever happens.

clue.text: Vain men? Failures, left out

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so the letter standing for left is dropped

blocks.note: flops are failures, especially shows that close early
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark that conceited men are failures who get excluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Fops are dandies excessively concerned with their clothes and appearance; the question mark flags a definition by description.

clue.text: Worth working on a style that's casual

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over and processed into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a way of doing something is a style

explanation.surface: Advice that it is worth developing a relaxed, informal manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A throwaway remark is offhand and said without emphasis, so it is casual in tone.

clue.text: Support objective story

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or chair
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Someone backing a factual, unbiased account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' reads as an adjective meaning unbiased, but it is the noun meaning goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale handed down, often unverified, so it is a kind of story.

clue.text: Slush and ice initially in projected outlook

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
in places the selected letter inside the phrase that follows it

blocks.note: something projected has been sent out
first letter of ice
a mentality is an outlook or way of thinking

explanation.surface: A weather report: slush and ice expected in the forecast outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a weather forecast; slush is in fact the definition, meaning mawkish sentiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Slush is a colloquial word for cloying, mawkish emotional material, which is excessive sentimentality.

clue.text: State in middle of daft business

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: the two central letters of daft
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: A government stuck in the middle of some silly commercial affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation in a silly business, but it is the verb to declare.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to declare something firmly as true, which is to state it.

clue.text: Drop unfinished argument in high voice

indicators.note: unfinished means the word lacks its final letter

blocks.note: to fall is to drop
a set-to is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: Someone breaking off an incomplete quarrel while speaking in a squeaky voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high register a male singer uses above his normal range.

clue.text: Adult insect I found on fruit without core

indicators.note: without core means the central letter of the fruit is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
a mango is a tropical fruit

explanation.surface: A naturalist reports finding a grown insect sitting on a piece of fruit with its core gone.
explanation.walkthrough: MANGO has five letters, so its core is the central N.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, sexually mature stage of an insect after metamorphosis, so the adult form.

clue.text: Game with glue and thin piece of wood

blocks.note: a match is a game or contest
to stick is to glue; with joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: A craft project: a game played using adhesive and slivers of wood, like a model kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchstick is the slender wooden stem of a match, used in model-making as a thin strip.

clue.text: Singer in broadcast finer than a lark

indicators.note: broadcast suggests seed scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast where a singer's voice is praised as finer than a lark's song.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is praise for a songbird of a voice; 'broadcast' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretha Franklin was the American soul vocalist known as the Queen of Soul.

clue.text: Standard silver working model

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A catalogue entry for a functioning standard silver model of some appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a product version, but it is the definition: a perfect example.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, a perfect example others should follow.

clue.text: Sadly alter in becoming dependent

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters end up badly out of order

blocks.note: the fodder, both words used

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that they have changed into a needy, dependent person.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliant means relying on someone or something for support, which is being dependent.

clue.text: Bear forlorn hope within one

indicators.note: forlorn means wretched and in a sorry state, so the following letters are disordered

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: An exhortation to endure despairing feelings inside oneself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the verb endure, but it names a famous bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's honey-loving teddy bear of the Hundred Acre Wood.

clue.text: Sensational exercises in street destroy our team

indicators.note: in places the exercises inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
St is the abbreviation for street
to undo is to ruin or destroy
us is our side, our team

explanation.surface: A sensational tale of street exercises that wreck the home side.
explanation.walkthrough: The exercises sit inside the run of three words that follow, not just inside the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupendous means astonishingly impressive, so it is a near synonym of sensational.

clue.text: Time connected with particular urban area

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
own means particular to oneself, as in their own

explanation.surface: A planning note about a time linked to some specific built-up area.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a built-up settlement larger than a village, so an urban area.

clue.text: Go with fellows and start to toil in field

indicators.note: start to picks out the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to depart is to go
fellows are men; with joins the pieces
first letter of toil

explanation.surface: Farm labourers leaving with the other men to start work in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks agricultural but is the definition: an area of activity or study.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a sphere of activity or expertise, in the same sense as a field of work.

clue.text: Wreckage of a ship seen in New Testament book

indicators.note: wreckage is something smashed apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, all three words used

explanation.surface: A shipwreck described in a book of the Bible, as Paul's was in Acts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesians is Paul's epistle to the church at Ephesus, one of the books of the New Testament.

clue.text: Vehicle owner terribly stressed

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A motorist who is terribly anxious, perhaps about a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Careworn means showing the strain of prolonged worry, so tired and stressed-looking.

clue.text: Financial officers in a mess, party in disarray

indicators.note: in disarray means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Treasurers left in a muddle, their political party in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Paymasters are officials responsible for paying out wages and funds, so financial officers.

clue.text: Elegant greeting in duplicate

indicators.note: in sets the greeting inside the abbreviation for a copy

blocks.note: cc, carbon copy, marks a duplicate
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A stylish salutation written out twice.
explanation.walkthrough: CC is the carbon copy line on a letter or email.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylishly fashionable, a close synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Poor bloke, not all right after charge

indicators.note: not all right means the letters standing for all right are missing

blocks.note: a fee is a charge
taken as written; OK, meaning all right, is taken out

explanation.surface: Sympathy for a man who is unwell after being arrested and charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the charge first; bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means weak or inadequate, as in a poor or feeble attempt.

clue.text: What's in bulletin about passion and heart of powerful All Blacks?

indicators.note: heart of asks for the central letters of the word that follows
about means surrounding, so the bulletin wraps round the following pieces

blocks.note: a news bulletin; the news
zeal is passion or fervour
taken as written
the two central letters of powerful

explanation.surface: A sports report on the passion and power of New Zealand's rugby team.
explanation.walkthrough: The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union team, so the definition is fair as a sample of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The All Blacks are players from New Zealand, so they are New Zealanders by nationality.

clue.text: Liquid consumed in wide river

indicators.note: in puts the eaten word inside the letters on either side

blocks.note: W is wide, an extra in cricket scoring
R is the abbreviation for river
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Fluid swallowed while crossing a broad river.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, scored W.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the commonest liquid of all, so it is a straightforward example of the class.

clue.text: Colour that's integral to juicy anecdote

indicators.note: integral to means forming part of, so the letters lie inside the phrase

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A shade that is vital to a racy story.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, one of the printing primaries.

clue.text: Revealed stake in remote settlement

blocks.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
a post is a stake driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A wooden stake uncovered at a far-flung frontier camp.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small settlement or station far from the main centres of population.

clue.text: Sign attached to your back room full of books

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the short form of your is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac
yr is a written abbreviation for your

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note: a star-sign plaque fixed to your rear room full of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back room' reads as one phrase, but back is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A library is a room or building housing a collection of books.

clue.text: Bound stem

blocks.note: first meaning: a leap, as a verb or noun
second meaning: to arise or originate from a source

explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions read naturally as verbs: to leap, and to originate, as in problems stem from a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump forward suddenly, and also to come from or originate, like a river from its source.

clue.text: One name for each child actually present

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for name
per means for each, as in per head
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A register-taking teacher noting one name per pupil who is actually in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in person means being physically there yourself rather than by proxy.
